**** 
69th Legislature 2025 SB 555.1
- 1 -  Authorized Print Version – SB 555 
1 SENATE BILL NO. 555
2 INTRODUCED BY V. RICCI
3
4 A BILL FOR AN ACT ENTITLED: “AN ACT GENERALLY REVISING GAMBLING LAWS; REVISING THE 
5 DEFINITION OF "INTERNET GAMBLING" TO INCLUDE ONLINE CASINOS; PROVIDING AN EXCEPTION 
6 FOR ONLINE CASINOS THAT DO NOT ALLOW THE USE OF CURRENCY OF ANY KIND; INCLUDING 
7 CRYPTOCURRENCY IN THE DEFINITION OF "INTERNET GAMBLING"; REVISING THE DISPOSAL OF 
8 FINES TO THE CREDIT OF THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE; REVISING CRIMINAL PENALTIES TO 
9 INCLUDE MISDEMEANOR AND FELONY CRIMES; AND AMENDING SECTIONS 23-5-112, 23-5-123, 23-5-
10 154, AND 23-5-162, MCA.”
11
12 BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MONTANA:
13
14Section 1. Section 23-5-112, MCA, is amended to read:
15 "23-5-112. Definitions. Unless the context requires otherwise, the following definitions apply to parts 
16 1 through 8 of this chapter:
17 (1) "Antique gambling device" means:
18 (a) an illegal gambling device manufactured prior to 1994; or
19 (b) any gambling device which, at any present time, is 30 years old or older.
20 (2) "Applicant" means a person who has applied for a license or permit issued by the department 
21 pursuant to parts 1 through 8 of this chapter.
22 (3) "Application" means a written request for a license or permit issued by the department. The 
23 department shall adopt rules describing the forms and information required for issuance of a license.
24 (4) "Associated gambling business" means a person who provides a service or product to a 
25 licensed gambling business and who:
26 (a) has a reason to possess or maintain control over gambling devices;
27 (b) has access to proprietary information or gambling tax information; or
28 (c) is a party in processing gambling transactions.
**** 
69th Legislature 2025 SB 555.1
- 2 -  Authorized Print Version – SB 555 
1 (5) "Authorized equipment" means, with respect to live keno or bingo, equipment that may be 
2 inspected by the department and that randomly selects the numbers.
3 (6) "Bingo" means a gambling activity played for prizes with a card bearing a printed design of 5 
4 columns. The letters B-I-N-G-O must appear above the design, with each letter above one of the columns. 
5 More than 75 numbers may not be used. One or more numbers may appear in each square, except for the 
6 center square, which may be considered a free play. Numbers must be randomly drawn using authorized 
7 equipment until the game is won by the person or persons who first cover one or more previously designated 
8 arrangements of numbers on the bingo card.
9 (7) "Bingo caller" means a person 18 years of age or older who, using authorized equipment, 
10 announces the order of the numbers drawn in live bingo.
11 (8) "Bingo session" means all activities incidental to a series of bingo games conducted by a 
12 licensed operator beginning when the first bingo ball is drawn in the first game of bingo.
13 (9) "Card game table" or "table" means a live card game table:
14 (a) authorized by permit and made available to the public on the premises of a licensed gambling 
15 operator; or
16 (b) operated by a senior citizen center.
17 (10) "Card game tournament" means a gambling activity for which a permit has been issued 
18 involving participants who pay valuable consideration for the opportunity to compete against each other in a 
19 series of live card games conducted over a designated period of time.
20 (11) "Dealer" means a person with a dealer's license issued under part 3 of this chapter.
21 (12) "Department" means the department of justice.
22 (13) "Distributor" means a person who:
23 (a) purchases or obtains from a licensed manufacturer, distributor, route operator, or operator 
24 equipment of any kind for use in gambling activities; and
25 (b) sells the equipment to a licensed manufacturer, distributor, route operator, or operator.
26 (14) (a) "Gambling" or "gambling activity" means risking any money, credit, deposit, check, property, 
27 or other thing of value for a gain that is contingent in whole or in part upon lot, chance, or the operation of a 
28 gambling device or gambling enterprise.
**** 
69th Legislature 2025 SB 555.1
- 3 -  Authorized Print Version – SB 555 
1 (b) The term does not mean conducting or participating in:
2 (i) promotional games of chance;
3 (ii) amusement games regulated by Title 23, chapter 6, part 1;
4 (iii) social card games of bridge, cribbage, hearts, pinochle, pitch, rummy, solo, and whist played 
5 solely for prizes of minimal value, as defined by department rule; or
6 (iv) patron dice games as defined in this section.
7 (15) "Gambling device" means a mechanical, electromechanical, or electronic device, machine, slot 
8 machine, instrument, apparatus, contrivance, scheme, or system used or intended for use in any gambling 
9 activity.
10 (16) "Gambling enterprise" means an activity, scheme, or agreement or an attempted activity, 
11 scheme, or agreement to provide gambling or a gambling device to the public.
12 (17) (a) "Gift enterprise" means a gambling activity in which persons have qualified to obtain 
13 property to be awarded by purchasing or agreeing to purchase goods or services.
14 (b) The term does not mean:
15 (i) a cash or merchandise attendance prize or premium that county fair commissioners of 
16 agricultural fairs and rodeo associations may give away at public drawings at fairs and rodeos;
17 (ii) a promotional game of chance;
18 (iii) an amusement game regulated under Title 23, chapter 6;
19 (iv) a savings promotion raffle offered by a bank, trust company, mutual savings bank, savings and 
20 loan association, or credit union authorized to do business and accept deposits in this state under state or 
21 federal law and conducted in compliance with 23-5-413 that entitles individual members or depositors equal 
22 chances to win a designated prize by depositing a sum of money during a specified savings period; or
23 (v) an entry into a raffle as a result of paying membership dues or making a purchase of an item 
24 offered during a fundraising event held by a nonprofit organization.
25 (18) "Gross proceeds" means gross revenue received less prizes paid out.
26 (19) "Heads or tails" means a gambling activity in which players attempt to predict the outcome of a 
27 coin toss. Those who are incorrect are eliminated and those who are correct continue to another round until one 
28 winning player remains and is awarded a prize.
**** 
69th Legislature 2025 SB 555.1
- 4 -  Authorized Print Version – SB 555 
1 (20) "House player" means a person participating in a card game who has a financial relationship 
2 with the operator, card room contractor, or dealer or who has received money or chips from the operator, card 
3 room contractor, or dealer to participate in a card game.
4 (21) "Illegal gambling device" means a gambling device not specifically authorized by statute or by 
5 the rules of the department. The term includes:
6 (a) a ticket or card, by whatever name known, containing concealed numbers or symbols that may 
7 match numbers or symbols designated in advance as prize winners, including a pull tab, punchboard, push 
8 card, tip board, pickle ticket, break-open, or jar game, except for one used under Title 23, chapter 7, under part 
9 5 of this chapter, in a bingo game approved by the department under part 4 of this chapter, or in a promotional 
10 game of chance approved by the department; and
11 (b) an apparatus, implement, or device, by whatever name known, specifically designed to be 
12 used in conducting an illegal gambling enterprise, including a faro box, faro layout, roulette wheel, roulette 
13 table, craps table, or slot machine, except as provided in 23-5-153.
14 (22) "Illegal gambling enterprise" means a gambling enterprise that violates or is not specifically 
15 authorized by a statute or a rule of the department. The term includes:
16 (a) a card game, by whatever name known, involving any bank or fund from which a participant 
17 may win money or other consideration and that receives money or other consideration lost by the participant 
18 and includes the card games of blackjack, twenty-one, jacks or better, baccarat, or chemin de fer;
19 (b) dice games known as craps, hazard, or chuck-a-luck, but not including patron dice games or 
20 activities authorized by 23-5-160;
21 (c) credit gambling; and
22 (d) internet gambling.
23 (23) (a) "Internet gambling", by whatever name known, includes but is not limited to the conduct of 
24 any legal or illegal gambling enterprise through the use of communications technology that allows a person 
25 using money, paper checks, electronic checks, electronic transfers of money, credit cards, debit cards, 
26 cryptocurrency, or any other instrumentality to transmit to a computer information to assist in the placing of a 
27 bet or wager and corresponding information related to the display of the game, game outcomes, or other similar 
28 information.
**** 
69th Legislature 2025 SB 555.1
- 5 -  Authorized Print Version – SB 555 
1 (b) (i) The term includes online casinos, by whatever name known, which constitute internet 
2 gambling and therefore are prohibited. This includes but is not limited to any platform, website, or application 
3 that knowingly transmits or receives gambling information, allows consumers to place a bet or wager using any 
4 form of currency, and makes payouts of any form of currency.
5 (ii) Online casinos that do not allow the use of currency of any kind are not considered a gambling 
6 activity and therefore are permitted.
7 (b)(c) The term does not include the operation of a simulcast facility or advance deposit wagering 
8 with a licensed advance deposit wagering hub operator allowed by Title 23, chapter 4, the state lottery provided 
9 for in Title 23, chapter 7, or a raffle authorized under Title 23, chapter 5, part 4, that is sponsored by a nonprofit 
10 organization and that is registered with the department. If all aspects of the gaming are conducted on Indian 
11 lands in conformity with federal statutes and with administrative regulations of the national Indian gaming 
12 commission, the term does not include class II gaming or class III gaming as defined by 25 U.S.C. 2703.
13 (24) "Keno" means a game of chance in which prizes are awarded using a card with 8 horizontal 
14 rows and 10 columns on which a player may pick up to 10 numbers. A keno caller, using authorized equipment, 
15 shall select at random at least 20 numbers out of numbers between 1 and 80, inclusive.
16 (25) "Keno caller" means a person 18 years of age or older who, using authorized equipment, 
17 announces the order of the numbers drawn in live keno.
18 (26) "License" means a license for an operator, dealer, card room contractor, manufacturer of 
19 devices not legal in Montana, sports tab game seller, manufacturer of electronic live bingo or keno equipment, 
20 other manufacturer, distributor, or route operator that is issued to a person by the department.
21 (27) "Licensee" means a person who has received a license from the department.
22 (28) "Live card game" or "card game" means a card game that is played in public between persons 
23 on the premises of a licensed gambling operator or in a senior citizen center.
24 (29) (a) "Lottery" means a scheme, by whatever name known, for the disposal or distribution of 
25 property among persons who have paid or promised to pay valuable consideration for the chance of obtaining 
26 the property or a portion of it or for a share or interest in the property upon an agreement, understanding, or 
27 expectation that it is to be distributed or disposed of by lot or chance.
28 (b) The term does not mean lotteries authorized under Title 23, chapter 7.
**** 
69th Legislature 2025 SB 555.1
- 6 -  Authorized Print Version – SB 555 
1 (30) "Manufacturer" means a person who:
2 (a) assembles from raw materials or subparts a completed piece of equipment or pieces of 
3 equipment of any kind to be used as a gambling device and who sells the equipment directly to a licensed 
4 distributor, route operator, or operator;
5 (b) possesses gambling devices or components of gambling devices for the purpose of testing 
6 them; or
7 (c) purchases gambling devices or components from licensed manufacturers, distributors, route 
8 operators, or operators as trade-ins or to refurbish, rebuild, or repair to sell to licensed manufacturers, 
9 distributors, route operators, or operators.
10 (31) "Nonprofit organization" means an organization established as a nonprofit to support charitable, 
11 religious, scholastic, educational, veterans', fraternal, beneficial, civic, senior citizens', or service organizations' 
12 charitable activities, scholarships or educational grants, or community service projects.
13 (32) "Operator" means a person who purchases, receives, or acquires, by lease or otherwise, and 
14 operates or controls for use in public a gambling device or gambling enterprise authorized under parts 1 
15 through 8 of this chapter.
16 (33) "Ownership" or "ownership interest" means the ability to:
17 (a) share in the profits, losses, or liabilities of a gambling operation;
18 (b) enjoy the privileges reserved to licensees; or
19 (c) control a gambling operation.
20 (34) (a) "Patron dice games" means dice games involving wagers played by two or more patrons 
21 over 18 years of age on the premises of a licensed gambling operator that the licensee does not promote and in 
22 which the licensee does not participate or acquire a financial interest either as the bank of the game or as the 
23 source of credit for players.
24 (b) The term does not include:
25 (i) an illegal gambling enterprise as defined in this section; or
26 (ii) activities authorized by 23-5-160.
27 (35) "Permit" means approval from the department to make available for public play a gambling 
28 device or gambling enterprise approved by the department pursuant to parts 1 through 8 of this chapter.
**** 
69th Legislature 2025 SB 555.1
- 7 -  Authorized Print Version – SB 555 
1 (36) "Person" or "persons" means both natural and artificial persons and all partnerships, 
2 corporations, associations, clubs, fraternal orders, and societies, including religious and charitable 
3 organizations.
4 (37) "Premises" means the physical building or property within or upon which a licensed gambling 
5 activity occurs, as stated on an operator's license application and approved by the department.
6 (38) "Promotional game of chance" means a scheme, by whatever name known, for the disposal or 
7 distribution of property among persons who have not paid or are not expected to pay any valuable 
8 consideration or who have not purchased or are not expected to purchase any goods or services for a chance 
9 to obtain the property, a portion of it, or a share in it. The property is disposed of or distributed by simulating a 
10 gambling enterprise authorized by parts 1 through 8 of this chapter or by operating a device or enterprise 
11 approved by the department that was manufactured or intended for use for purposes other than gambling.
12 (39) "Public gambling" means gambling conducted in:
13 (a) a place, building, or conveyance to which the public has access or may be permitted to have 
14 access;
15 (b) a place of public resort, including but not limited to a facility owned, managed, or operated by a 
16 partnership, corporation, association, club, fraternal order, or society, including a religious or charitable 
17 organization; or
18 (c) a place, building, or conveyance to which the public does not have access if players are 
19 publicly solicited or the gambling activity is conducted in a predominantly commercial manner.
20 (40) "Raffle" means a form of lottery in which each participant pays valuable consideration for a 
21 ticket to become eligible to win a prize. Winners must be determined by a random selection process approved 
22 by department rule.
23 (41) "Route operator" means a person who:
24 (a) purchases from a licensed manufacturer, route operator, or distributor equipment of any kind 
25 for use in a gambling activity;
26 (b) leases the equipment to a licensed operator for use by the public; and
27 (c) may sell to a licensed operator equipment that had previously been authorized to be operated 
28 on a premises and may sell gambling equipment to a distributor or manufacturer.
**** 
69th Legislature 2025 SB 555.1
- 8 -  Authorized Print Version – SB 555 
1 (42) "Senior citizen center" means a facility operated by a nonprofit or governmental organization 
2 that provides services to senior citizens in the form of daytime or evening educational or recreational activities 
3 and does not provide living accommodations to senior citizens. Services qualifying under this definition must be 
4 recognized in the state plan on aging adopted by the department of public health and human services.
5 (43) (a) "Slot machine" means a mechanical, electrical, electronic, or other gambling device, 
6 contrivance, or machine that, upon insertion of a coin, currency, token, credit card, or similar object or upon 
7 payment of any valuable consideration, is available to play or operate, the play or operation of which, whether 
8 by reason of the skill of the operator or application of the element of chance, or both, may deliver or entitle the 
9 person playing or operating the gambling device to receive cash, premiums, merchandise, tokens, or anything 
10 of value, whether the payoff is made automatically from the machine or in any other manner.
11 (b) This definition does not apply to video gambling machines authorized under part 6 of this 
12 chapter.
13 (44) "Video gambling machine" is a gambling device specifically authorized by part 6 of this chapter 
14 and the rules of the department."
15
16Section 2. Section 23-5-123, MCA, is amended to read:
17 "23-5-123. Disposal of fines and penalties for violation of gambling laws. All fines and penalties 
18 collected by criminal, civil, or administrative process for a violation of a provision of parts 1 through 8 of this 
19 chapter or a rule of the department must be deposited in the state general fund operating budget of the 
20 department of justice."
21
22Section 3. Section 23-5-154, MCA, is amended to read:
23 "23-5-154. Soliciting participation in illegal gambling activity prohibited. A person who purposely 
24 or knowingly advertises for or solicits another person to participate in an illegal gambling enterprise or use an 
25 illegal gambling device is guilty of a misdemeanor crime and is punishable under 23-5-161 and 23-5-162."
26
27Section 4. Section 23-5-162, MCA, is amended to read:
28 "23-5-162. Criminal liabilities -- felony. (1) A person who purposely or knowingly violates a provision 
**** 
69th Legislature 2025 SB 555.1
- 9 -  Authorized Print Version – SB 555 
1 of parts 1 through 8 of this chapter, the punishment for which is a felony, may upon conviction be fined not 
2 more than $50,000 or imprisoned for not more than 10 years, or both, for each violation.
3 (2) In addition to any penalty imposed under subsection (1), the department shall revoke all 
4 licenses or permits issued to the person under parts 1 through 8 of this chapter and may not issue the person 
5 another license or permit under parts 1 through 8 of this chapter.
6 (3) A person who purposely or knowingly operates any type of illegal internet gambling site within 
7 the state's borders, including operating an online gambling site in the state through licensed or unlicensed 
8 offshore sources, is subject to felony criminal liabilities as provided under this section."
9 - END -
